reason: The rationale states 'Section 41 designates the United Architects of the Philippines (UAP) as the accredited... IAPOA'. This is incorrect. Section 4 of RA 9266 designates IAPOA/UAP as the nominating organization, NOT Section 41. Section 41 is about IRR adoption. This matches the error pattern warned about in the article.

proposed.text: What is the role of the IAPOA (now United Architects of the Philippines, Inc.) in relation to the PRC and PRBoA?

options.text: The IAPOA is the same as the PRC, functioning as a regulatory body for architects.

The IAPOA is a professional association distinct from government regulatory bodies; under Section 4 it nominates PRBoA members, provides input on standards, and may offer self-regulatory functions complementary to government regulation.
The IAPOA has complete regulatory authority over architects, including licensing and disciplinary actions.
The IAPOA has no role in professional regulation, focusing solely on member services and advocacy.

rationale.a: The IAPOA is a professional association; the PRC is a government agency.
rationale.c: The IAPOA has consultative input but not complete regulatory authority.
rationale.d: The IAPOA plays significant roles in nomination, input, and complementary regulation.
rationale.correct: Section 4 of RA 9266 designates the United Architects of the Philippines (UAP) as the accredited Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA). Its roles include nomination of PRBoA members, CPD input, and consultation on standards. Note: Section 41 is about IRR adoption, NOT about IAPOA designation.
rationale.takeaway: Professional regulation involves dual systems: government regulation (through PRC/PRBoA) and professional association self-regulation (through IAPOA). Section 4, not Section 41, governs the IAPOA role.
